action.name: Padless HyperBoost firmware auto-exit negative control on USB-C 100 W
action.value: Apply paired mode 7 once on FullPower330W, switch to USB-C 100 W, observe paired thermal state for ten seconds without an OpenBlade disable, then reconnect full power and restore the exact Balanced baseline

validation.applyResult: Applied successfully once from the confirmed Balanced and Automatic baseline on FullPower330W.
validation.readbackResult: The firmware did not exit HyperBoost: paired mode 7 remained active for all twenty UsbCPower100W samples without an OpenBlade disable.
validation.restorationResult: After FullPower330W was freshly reconfirmed, one bounded paired cleanup restored the saved Balanced state.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: Exact Balanced restoration and final physical pad absence were confirmed with no indeterminate write or manual recovery state.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: The validator used the hash-pinned ten-second boundary plan with 500 ms cadence, no OpenBlade disable during observation, and full-power reconnection before cleanup.
After paired mode-7 confirmation, the adapter classified as UsbCPower100W for the complete observation while both thermal channels remained in mode 7. Firmware auto-exit was not observed.
After the negative observation, FullPower330W was freshly confirmed before one two-channel Balanced cleanup and exact readback.
The private transcript remains uncommitted; this annotation retains its hash and length plus the exact Capture executable and final read-only Balanced confirmation.

limitations: This is authoritative negative evidence for firmware auto-exit on the tested transition: mode 7 persisted for ten seconds on UsbCPower100W.
Persistent semantic mode 7 does not by itself prove that elevated CPU or GPU power limits remained available on USB-C.
The test begins on admitted full power and does not test whether firmware accepts a new HyperBoost command submitted while already on USB-C.
The result is scoped to the exact RZ09-0581, BIOS 4.00 evidence provenance, Balanced and Automatic baseline, and confirmed physical cooling-pad absence.

productionAdmission.reason: Firmware left paired mode 7 active throughout the complete USB-C 100 W observation. The reviewed policy accepts HyperBoost persistence on any external-power class and relies on the separately confirmed firmware exit when external power is removed.

notes: The OpenBlade service and competing Razer applications remained inactive.
No Razer service was started, stopped, or restored.
